text:
I feel like this is a tricky one because to me, it’s almost their signature to pack a lot of different sounds in an album but then tie it together thematically. I think it’s one of the things that drew me to BTS is this sort of relentless drive to look at the same subject through a thousand different lenses and moods and sounds. It makes this kind of hall of mirrors effect that feels both conceptual and personal.

I feel that in Wings (my beloved), MOTS7, and even HYYH, especially HYYH 2 I think is my pick for musically diverse (we got Butterfly and Baepsae on the same album!) but also incredibly culturally significant and thematically consistent.  It did capture Youth in a way that could span across all its ups and downs. 

On the other hand, the most sonically coherent to me would be Be (Dynamite excluded) and while I adore some songs on it (Blue and Gray especially) I do miss that kind of cornucopia feel that to me is almost a trademark.
thread_title: Which BTS albums are culturally more important, than they are musically cohesive?

text:
What an amazing question! Without a doubt, WINGS and Map of the Soul are the two albums I feel shaped BTS’s identity the most and also create such connection with army. WINGS is such a deep and meaningful album, and I think it marked a major turning point in their careers, both musically and artistically. Then we have MAP OF THE SOUL, which explored deeper themes of identity, and self reflection, which I feel resonated with a lot of people.

Now, one album that I feel didn’t quite come together as cohesively as some of their previous releases is ARIRANG. That doesn’t mean it’s a bad album at all. Based on what I’ve seen online, I can understand why some ARMYs felt a disconnect with it. Personally, though, I enjoyed the album. After so many years without having BTS together again, I think what matters most is that they’re back, healthy, and able to make music together. More than anything, I genuinely hope they’re happy and healthy. They’ve given us so much over the years, and I hope they get to enjoy this chapter of their lives just as much as we’ve enjoyed being part of their journey.  How about you? Loved the question
thread_title: Which BTS albums are culturally more important, than they are musically cohesive?

text:
I will prob get flack for this but MOTS: 7. Due to the timing, and what happened soon after its release, I think it is revered in the fandom. There are standout tracks on it, many of which were not performed in concert for awhile, kind of amping their status. "On" and "Black Swan" both feel culturally big, with their multiple music videos and for the former, epic vibe. But I don't really find the album itself musically cohesive and very rarely listen to it as an album. 

We are probably past the solo songs on BTS albums era, at least to the that degree, but I think LY: Answer handled them best. A rerelease with additional tracks vs seven solo tracks on one album (which I think worked on Wings better).
